title: Where churches disagree today
hookLine: on sexuality and gender, churches reach sincerely different conclusions; the path won't rank them

cards: Thanksgiving dinner. Two cousins, raised in the same church, both still praying, both reading the same Bible.

Somebody mentions a wedding, and the table goes quiet, because the cousins have landed in different places on a question about sexuality, and each got there by praying and reading. Neither one is faking.

This week has walked through peace and war, money, work, marriage and singleness. It ends at a place where churches feel strain. On sexuality and gender, Christians reach sincerely different conclusions.

teach.b: Here's the shape of it, as fairly as it can be put. Some churches teach that marriage is between a man and a woman, and that sex belongs inside it.

They point to Genesis, to Jesus quoting Genesis on marriage, and to passages in Paul, and they hold that the church should keep teaching what it has received, while saying that everyone is welcome to come and worship.
Other churches bless same-sex marriages and open every part of church life, including leadership, to gay and transgender members.

They also point to scripture: to Jesus welcoming those others pushed to the edge, and to times the early church changed course, like the decision in Acts to welcome Gentiles without requiring circumcision.
Some people sit somewhere between, or are still unsure. Both sides are reading the Bible. Both are trying to be faithful.
These questions have split denominations and strained families, and the hurt runs on more than one side. So what does the tradition offer for the disagreement itself?
Paul, writing to a church divided over food and holy days, said: "Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another."
To the Ephesians he wrote of "speaking the truth in love." Both halves count: truth as each side sees it, and love that doesn't leave the table.

teach.h: IF YE HAVE LOVE ONE TO ANOTHER.
teach.b: And Jesus named a mark that should still show through any argument: "By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another." Not if you agree. If you love.

how: Churches discuss questions of sexuality and gender in synods, conventions, councils and congregational meetings; some have reaffirmed traditional teaching, some have changed their practice, and some allow congregations to differ.

games.q: what does “where churches disagree today” mean?
o: where Christians reach different views on sexuality
the old split between Catholics and Protestants
debates over which Bible translation is correct

games.q: the shape of the disagreement — tap the pairs.
p: teach what they received on marriage
if ye have love one to another

s: churches that disagree do so because one side ignores the Bible
both sides read scripture and pray. they reach sincerely different conclusions.
Paul wrote to a church divided over food and holy days
Romans 14: "follow after the things which make for peace."
Jesus says his disciples will be known by agreeing
"by this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another."

games.q: you're one of the cousins at Thanksgiving. the table has gone quiet. what does the tradition's own advice point toward?
o: speak the truth as you see it, in love, and stay.
games.why: Paul's line is "speaking the truth in love," and Jesus's mark of a disciple is love one to another. neither tells you to leave the table.

practice: Bring to mind someone you disagree with on a question like this, a relative, a friend, a pastor, someone in your church, and instead of rehearsing your case, try to name honestly what they're trying to be faithful to.
Stay with that for a few breaths, then think of your own church's conversations, wherever it stands. If you pray, you can pray for the people having them.

wordCard.voice: Where churches disagree today. On sexuality and gender, Christians reach sincerely different conclusions from the same Bible. This path names them and ranks none.

orig.note: Greek, Ephesians 4:15: speaking the truth in love.

carryVoice: Your line: love in disagreement. Truth as each sees it, and a seat at the table. That's the week.
